newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 11.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 11.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST......
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

LONDON - Britain's Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc says its share of independent television advertising revenue is not satisfactory and it is determined to restore it to past levels. YTT says its 1996 advertising sales were "disappointing", falling to 10.31 percent of total ITV advertising revenue -- more than 12 million pounds ($19.3 million) below expectations at the start of the year.

DALLAS - The Beef Board, which markets beef for U.S. cattle producers, will increase its budget by $2 million to $47.5 million in 1997. The funds will be used to promote beef to consumers, food service operators and health professionals.

DES MOINES, Iowa. - MidAmerican Energy Co is launching a $2.2 million advertising campaign to establish its brand identity. The campaign is being handled by Clarity Coverdale Fury, a Minneapolis advertising agency. *********
ZAGREB - Ivana Trump, former wife of American tycoon Donald Trump, met Croatian government officials to discuss promoting Croatian tourism, the state agency HINA reports.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc says it has no comment on a French newspaper report that it might become a shareholder of the French media group Havas. Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier says that Havas would like an Anglo-Saxon investor as a way to bolster its presence on the other side of the Atlantic.

BRUSSELS - The European Commission is seeking industry comments on a European digital pay-radio business operated by Sony Digital Radio Europe Ltd. Music Choice Europe programmes around 60 channels of non-stop music for distribution to homes across Europe. The channels are transmitted via cable operators but they are expected to be made available to customers through satellite broadcasting direct to homes "in the near future", the Commission says.

PARIS - France's Pathe declines comment on a newspaper report that it might sell its 17 percent stake in British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc. However, a Pathe spokesman says the company is satisfied with the performance of BSkyB.

LONDON - The ITV commercial television network says four million Britons tuned in to watch the Australian Formula One Grand Prix this weekend. ITV, screening its first Grand Prix, paid an estimated 70 million pounds to secure a five-year deal for live coverage of Formula One racing. It was previously broadcast by the BBC.

NEW YORK - MCI Communications Corp is launching a national, on-line game service in the U.S. The service lets personal computer users play popular computer games against other personal computer users.

BADEN-BADEN, Germany. - Computer giant IBM Corp says its German unit has formed a partnership with broadcaster Suedwestfunk to develop Internet-related ventures. The two plan to develop a virtual shopping mall on the Internet where computer users will be able to purchase IBM products and items related to Suedwestfunk programming.

MIAMI - Durex Consumer Products plans to promote Durex Sheik condoms by bringing actress Carmen Electra, from the television series "Baywatch," to Panama City, Florida, to tutor student fun-seekers on the benefits of using condoms. Electra "will help show them that condoms are a normal, fun part of healthy relationships," the company says.

MUNICH - Adidas AG Chairman Robert Louis-Dreyfus says the company is on the way to becoming the "best sports brand in the world". The German sports retailer says record sales lifted group operating profit to 360 million marks ($211.4 million) in 1996 from 243 million marks the year before. *********

STOCKHOLM - Volvo Cars says it aims to increase car sales in Europe this year. "Our aim is to increase our sales in Europe to nearly 230,000 cars compared with last year's volume of 216,100 cars," says a spokesman. *********

LONDON - British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc plans to roll out self-scanning in up to 100 stores this year. The company started trials of self-scanning -- where customers use a hand-held machine to register the cost of their own shopping -- last November. The aim is to cut down checkout queues.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

FRANKFURT - Germans spend an average of three hours a day in front of their television sets, ZDF a German media research group says. It adds that Germany is the most competitive region among comparable television markets, with the average home able to receive 33 channels.

RIO DE JANEIRO - Brazilians are expected to munch their way through 14,000 tonnes of Easter eggs and chocolate bunnies this year, eight percent up on last year's 13,000 tonnes, industry officials say. Brazilians are not only scoffing down locally-made goodies but also imported products such as Ferrero Rocher and Kinder eggs.
